direct.title: Direct: the maestro writes the code
direct.when: Strong-model tokens are plentiful and the work is one lane, or it needs judgement no brief can pin down (unsettled design, a hard bug, performance, an unfamiliar codebase).
direct.cost: High strong-model tokens; the shortest path for one lane.
tasks: Goal: restate it with the smallest change that meets it
Baseline: base SHA, gates run once
Reproduce or specify: failing test for a bug, done-means assertions for a feature, a measured number for performance
Shape: data shapes and states before logic; remove before adding
Build in verifiable units, each ending in a passing check
Prove: gates by exit code, then drive the real artifact and keep the evidence
Self-review the whole diff as its reviewer would, then commit on the working branch
Independent review scaled by risk (first reviewer for ordinary work, the whole panel for high-risk); arbitrate every finding
Harden: promote agreed findings and corrections (references/hardening.md)
Report with the fixed block: GOAL / CHANGE / EVIDENCE / REVIEW / FINDINGS / HARDENED / OPEN
rules: Spend spare tokens on verification first, then the reviewer panel for high-risk changes, then a bake-off for a design fork with no precedent.
More than one lane is a delegate mode's work: ask the user whether frontier or economy.

frontier.title: Frontier: the session's model conducts strong coders
frontier.when: Ordinary code, plenty of strong-model tokens, and work that splits into lanes.
frontier.cost: Highest total tokens; best quality per lane and the most parallelism.
tasks: Plan: rulings for every ambiguity, lanes with the files each owns, shared hotspots assigned
Brief each lane (scripts/brief.mjs)
Spawn one executor per lane in its own worktree, tracked; record session ids
Answer blocked questions in the same session
Scope-check, then commit (the maestro commits)
Independent review, and verification on that commit in parallel: gates, plus runtime evidence where it can run (references/verification.md)
Arbitrate every finding; tag each agreed one with a category
Fix with a fresh executor and a fix brief; re-review in the reviewer's own session
Integrate the batch; review the integrated commit; merge small batches
Harden: promote recurring categories (references/hardening.md)
rules: A strong executor still gets exact rulings and an owned file map: parallel writers need them whatever their model.
The maestro writes no feature code in this mode, except a change small enough to do inline (one file and under ~50 changed lines).

critical.title: Critical: strong coders, red team on the plan and on the commit
critical.when: Building or changing code that moves money or value, grants authority, handles keys or secrets, or is a smart contract; and anything the user calls critical.
critical.cost: The most expensive build mode: strong coders only, two security passes, property tests required.
tasks: Plan: rulings, the invariants in plain statements, trust boundaries, lanes with the files each owns (smart contracts: run scripts/toolcheck.sh contracts first and name what is missing)
Red team the plan (references/redteam.md); resolve every agreed finding and re-issue the plan before any code
Brief each lane (scripts/brief.mjs); done-means carries a property or invariant test for every invariant the lane touches
Spawn one executor per lane in its own worktree, tracked; record session ids
Answer blocked questions in the same session
Scope-check, then commit (the maestro commits)
Independent review, and verification on that commit in parallel: gates, property tests, runtime evidence (references/verification.md)
Arbitrate every finding; fix with a fresh executor and a fix brief; re-review in the reviewer's own session
Integrate; red team the integrated commit; confirm each reproduction in a scratch worktree at that SHA
Fix agreed security findings with a fresh executor; the red-team reviewer that raised each re-checks it, and the reviewer re-reviews the fix diff, on the new SHA
Merge only when every agreed plan finding is resolved, and the review and the red team are both clear on the exact SHA being merged
Harden: every agreed security category becomes a check on its first occurrence (references/hardening.md)
rules: No cheap coders and no inline exception: every change goes through a brief, a review and the red team.
Anything that parses, validates or gates refuses malformed, incomplete or contradictory input; an exception refuses.
Smart contracts: local and forked chains only. No live-network transaction and no private key in the session.
Propose the audit mode before a first deployment or release, and after a large change to value-moving or authority logic.

economy.title: Economy: the session's model conducts cheap coders
economy.when: Saving strong-model tokens: many similar features, plumbing, schemas, CRUD, UI, mechanical refactors behind exact rulings.
economy.cost: Lowest strong-model tokens per feature; more wall-clock and more fix rounds.
tasks: Plan: rulings for every ambiguity, lanes with the files each owns, each lane routed by risk
Brief each lane completely (scripts/brief.mjs): the executor knows nothing the brief does not say
Spawn one executor per lane in its own worktree, tracked; record session ids
Answer blocked questions in the same session
Scope-check, then commit (the maestro commits)
Independent review, and verification on that commit in parallel: gates, plus runtime evidence where it can run (references/verification.md)
Arbitrate every finding; tag each agreed one with a category
Fix with a fresh executor and a fix brief; re-review in the reviewer's own session
Integrate the batch; review the integrated commit; merge small batches
Harden: promote recurring categories (references/hardening.md); record cost in the ledger
rules: High-risk work goes to executorStrong from the start.
A component class that needed 3 or more fix rounds on the cheap executor moves to executorStrong next time.
The maestro writes no feature code in this mode, except a change small enough to do inline (one file and under ~50 changed lines).

reserve.title: Reserve: no strong-model credits left
reserve.when: The model you normally conduct with is out of credits. Run the skill from Codex or OpenCode on the best model still available; cheap models code.
reserve.cost: No strong-model tokens. Slower, with smaller lanes and a review on everything.
tasks: Plan: rulings for every ambiguity; lanes of one package and under ~200 changed lines
Brief each lane completely (scripts/brief.mjs), with the full checklist areas it touches
Spawn one executor per lane in its own worktree, tracked; record session ids
Answer blocked questions in the same session
Scope-check, then commit (the maestro commits)
Independent review on every commit, trivial ones included
Arbitrate every finding; tag each agreed one with a category
Fix with a fresh executor and a fix brief; re-review in the reviewer's own session
Integrate and merge one feature at a time
List what should be re-reviewed by a strong model when credits return
rules: High-risk work needs the user's go-ahead in this mode: ask once, naming the parts; parts not approved are parked with a written note.
No risk tier skips review here: a weaker maestro's rulings need the second opinion more.
Three fix rounds on one component: stop and park it, do not start a fourth.

redteam.title: Red team: security check of a plan or a commit
redteam.when: On request, or proposed by the maestro: before committing to a design that crosses trust boundaries, and on the integrated commit of high-risk work.
redteam.cost: Read-only reviewers; no code is changed. Cost scales with the size of the scope given.
tasks: Scope: the exact plan revision or commit SHA, and the trust boundaries it crosses
Write the review prompt with the grounding (requirements, rulings, contracts) and the areas to cover
Dispatch each red-team reviewer read-only, in parallel; record session ids

Confirm each reproduction. A commit: run the reviewer's test in a scratch worktree at the reviewed SHA; it must fail there. A plan: check that the stated sequence of calls or inputs really follows from the rulings
Arbitrate the union of findings: AGREE with an exact ruling, or DISAGREE / DEFER with a reason
Hand agreed findings to a build mode as fix briefs; keep each reproduction as a regression test
Re-check each fix in the session of the reviewer that raised it, on the new SHA or plan revision
Harden: name the check each agreed category needs; the check itself is written in the build mode that fixes the finding (references/hardening.md)
Report: scope, areas covered and not covered, findings by severity, verdict, what is still open
rules: This mode changes no product code. Fixes go through a build mode, with the strongest coder that mode has.
An area that could not be covered is reported as not covered, never as clean.
Review the user's own code and systems only.

audit.title: Audit: a full security review of a contract system or a critical API
audit.when: Before a first deployment or release of a contract system, or of an API that moves money or grants authority; after a large change to its value-moving or authority logic; or on request.
audit.cost: The most expensive review: analyzers, a reviewer panel, property tests and a proof for every finding. Read-only on the code under review.
tasks: Before starting: confirm the target is the user's own code; run scripts/toolcheck.sh contracts|api|all; name the missing tools and skills
Scope: SHA, files in scope, specification, privileged roles, trust assumptions (scope.md)
Context: actors, assets, every entry point in one table, integrations, the invariants I1..In (context.md)
Deterministic pass: every analyzer available; triage results into candidates; a missing tool is 'not covered'
Panel review: each red-team model read-only, every area read by two model families
Properties: each invariant becomes a fuzz, invariant or property test in a scratch worktree
Specification against code: one row per claim (spec.md)
Prove every candidate: confirmed with a failing test, rejected with a reason, or unconfirmed with what would settle it
Report: severity, coverage table, invariants, spec table, residual risk (report.md)
Fix and re-check: fixes go through critical unless the user picks another build mode; each fix re-checked on the new SHA by the reviewer that raised it; search for siblings
Harden: name the detector, lint rule or invariant test each confirmed class needs; it is written in the build mode that fixes the finding
rules: Read-only on the code under review; tests and proofs live in a scratch worktree.
Local and forked chains only. No live-network transaction, no private key or seed phrase in the session.
Nothing is installed unasked. A missing analyzer is named and its checks are reported as not covered. A missing skill is named; its phase is still done, by the method in references/audit.md.
The report certifies nothing: it says what was looked for and what was found, and what an independent audit should look at first.

harden.title: Harden: make the repository hard to get wrong
harden.when: After a run of features, when the same findings keep returning, or before letting agents work with less review.
harden.cost: Mostly small, mechanical changes; cleanup lanes can go to cheap coders.
tasks: Collect categories: the ledger's findings column, the project checklist, recent review reports, corrections the user has repeated
Rank by recurrence and risk; take the top few, not all
For each, pick the highest rung of the ladder that fits: impossible by structure, static rule, test, runtime check
Write the rule with a message that tells the reader the root-cause fix
Clean the existing occurrences in the same batch, or record a baseline that may only go down
Wire the rule into the gates the briefs already run
Delete the prose line the rule replaces
Fill gaps in the feature map and the driver, when the user asked for it or agrees (references/verification.md)
Independent review of the rules: do they catch the original finding, do they block legitimate code
Report: category -> check, occurrences cleaned, prose removed, what stays as judgement
rules: When the user names the categories, do those and nothing else; collecting and ranking are for an open-ended request.
A new rule is proven by a test or sample that fails without it.
Large cleanups are lanes: brief them for this mode's executor (references/delegate.md).
Prose is deleted from the project's own checklist or instruction file; the skill's files are never edited.
